events.title: The Mishnah records the debates
events.text: rabbinic discussion of individual books (Ecclesiastes 'defiles the hands' — touches — but was included) as the Tanakh settled across the Second Temple period and after

events.title: Athanasius's Easter letter
events.text: the twenty-seven-book New Testament list appears — the boundary drawn by argument about apostolicity and use in worship

events.title: Council of Carthage
events.text: affirmed again — centuries of argument, not a committee's arbitrary pick

events.title: Uthman's standardisation
events.text: the Qurʾan, revealed orally over some twenty-two years, compiled into a standard text — authority resting on unbroken chains of recitation as much as on manuscripts

activities.anchor: reached their present form the same way
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a canon briefing
activities.name: scrCanonSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on canon formation is wrong — click it:
lines: The Hebrew canon settled across the Second Temple period and after, with individual books debated in the Mishnah.
The twenty-seven-book list appears in Athanasius's Easter letter of 367 and was affirmed at Hippo and Carthage.
The Qurʾan was standardised under Uthman within roughly two decades, its authority resting on unbroken chains of recitation.
Both scriptures reached their present form as a fixed list from the start.
config.correction: Canon is the community's first interpretation — closure's route and speed differ tellingly, and neither picture (fixed list from the start, or arbitrary committee pick) is documented.
config.why: Which texts count decides in advance what the tradition can hear — canon is interpretation before any verse is read.

activities.caption: file each belief-structure under its tradition
activities.name: scrBeliefSort

config.prompt: Doctrine as settled interpretation — file each structure:

items.label: 'begotten, not made' — fixed at Nicaea (325) against Arius's alternative
the six articles of faith — God, angels, revealed books, messengers, the Last Day, divine decree
the five roots of Usul ad-Din in Twelver Shiʿism
the Five Pillars resting on the Sunnah and graded isnad
covenants with Abraham, sealed at Sinai, and the Davidic promise

config.why: In all three cases, doctrine is the settled residue of interpretive practice — readings selected, argued over and institutionalised.

activities.anchor: Judaism treats interpretation as sanctified argument
activities.caption: pair each PaRDeS level with what it reads for
activities.name: scrPardesMatch

config.prompt: The fourfold scheme of Jewish reading — pair each level:
config.why: The interpretive tradition is revelation, not mere commentary: midrash exploits the text's gaps, and the Talmud records the dissenting view rather than erasing it — 'these and these are the words of the living G-d'.

activities.anchor: Christianity's history is a sequence of hermeneutics
activities.caption: true or false — the modern methods
activities.name: scrHermJudge

statements.s: Historical criticism reads the Bible as documents with dates, sources and agendas.
statements.why: Source criticism (Pentateuch sources; the Q source), form criticism, redaction criticism — philology matured into method.

statements.s: Fundamentalism's literalism is itself a modern style, born in reaction against critical scholarship.
statements.why: The scholars' noted irony: a stubborn text did not exist before there was a method to resist.

statements.s: The classical 'closing of the gates' of ijtihad is now doubted by historians.
statements.why: The gates of scholarly debate demonstrably never fully shut.

statements.s: Printed Qurʾan translations are treated as the revelation itself.
statements.why: They are titled 'interpretations of the meanings' — the Arabic Qurʾan is the revelation, and the compromise tells you where the community located the sacred.

activities.caption: fill the blank — the boundary controls
activities.name: scrBoundaryCloze

config.text: In practice every tradition has stringent boundary controls — recognised interpreters, accepted methods, %%0%%, chains of transmission.
config.hint: The institution the word 'boundary' implies: the enforcement mechanism between accepted and rejected readings.

activities.anchor: The fourfold sense is best learned by running it
activities.caption: walk the Reformation's challenge
activities.name: scrAuthorityBranch

config.root: The fourfold method's modern vulnerability, which the Reformation pressed: once the plain sense in the vernacular became available — who authorises the allegory?

start.text: The plain text now reaches every reader in the vernacular. What does the fourfold structure require to keep running?

choices.label: An interpreter with authority — the method cannot run itself
choices.feedback: Which is exactly the argument the tradition has been having ever since.

choices.label: Nothing — the text now interprets itself
choices.feedback: In practice the plain text immediately required philology, which matured into historical criticism.

end.text: Every tradition must solve the same problem — who may say what the text means — and differ only in where the authority sits: office, consensus, lineage, or text read within community.

config.why: Sola scriptura did not end interpretation — it relocated it: Scripture read within the community, with creeds and confessions as subordinate standards.

activities.anchor: Textual criticism operates underneath all of this
activities.caption: call the manuscript gap
activities.name: scrScrollsEst

config.prompt: The Dead Sea Scrolls, found from 1947, are roughly how many years older than the Leningrad Codex of 1008?
config.why: About a thousand years older — yet together they show a remarkably stable text with genuine variants: Jeremiah, for instance, runs substantially shorter in the Greek Septuagint.
